correctness_confidence.basis: Checked by hand: Lemma 4 (eqs. 4-6), Lemma 5 (eqs. 7-8, including F^(k-1)(1) = (-1)^(k-1)(k-1)! n m_k), Prop. 6 (Cesaro test, eqs. 9-11), the parameter limits and the explicit numerics of Sec. 4 (eq. 12, Ka >= 21/5, B < 1/(5n)), Cor. 8 (Newton identity), Thm. 3 moments (1/16 - 1/8 + 3/16 = 1/8), Thm. 11 algebra (X, Y, eq. 18, eq. 19) and the identity P'(0)=P'(1)/P(1). All of these hold. Theorem 2 was not checked beyond its outline. Minor algebra error in Sec. 2: B'/B - 3 equals -3z(z-1)^2/(z^3+1), not -3(z-1)^2/(z^3+1); this does not affect the limit. Theorem 2's upper-bound proof is a sketch, not a checked argument.

rigor.basis: Theorem 1 (Prop. 6) and Cor. 8 are argued in full. Theorem 2 relies on Lemma 10 (cone argument, plausible), an implicit-function step, and 'uniform' O(.) estimates that are asserted rather than shown; the paper itself says its constants are not explicit and not uniform in K. Theorem 3 upper bound asserts the secondary-maximum inequality (1+c)^6/[729(1-c)^2] < 1 and the global outer-arc bound without derivation. Theorem 11 'uniform O(.)' local/outer estimates are sketched.

novelty.basis: Thm. 1 gives s_n >= exp(-C sqrt(n)) and the explicit exp(-3 sqrt(n)) bound, which strengthens the restricted-slope bound of Tan et al. (arXiv:2608.02043, r_n >= exp(-(1+o(1)) sqrt(n) log n), confirmed from its abstract) because s_n <= r_n. Cor. 8 strengthens the Luo-Yang-Zhu result (arXiv:2607.22017: max_k |sum z_j^k| > e^(-lambda n) for every lambda > 0, confirmed from its abstract). The paper credits both. Thm. 3 (limit 1/sqrt(8) for the on-circle infimum) and Thm. 11 (one interior zero suffices) are presented as new; I did not search exhaustively for prior work on these, so novelty is not established.

significance.basis: The one-interior-zero threshold and the 1/sqrt(8) on-circle barrier are clean, well-motivated results about exterior/circle-root residuals with a link to Erdos Problem 973. The superalgebraic-decay claim (Thm. 2) would be significant if fully verified, but its proof is not checked. The paper states that the optimal rates for s_n, r_n and the one-root decay are open.

reproducibility.basis: The explicit constructions are given in closed form, so they can be reproduced. I ran a numerical check in my own sandbox from the text alone (not from any other file): for the Thm. 3 family P = B_t^m (1+z)^k the residual ratio goes to 0.3537 (m=1000, k=0) against the claimed 1/sqrt(8)=0.35355; for the Thm. 11 family the identities P'(0)=P'(1)/P(1), sum v^2 = 0 and sum v^3 = 0 hold to about 1e-10, and the residual decreases from 0.349 (n=341) to 0.115 (n=34001), roughly n^(-0.21) over this range. This supports the claims but does not establish the rate O(n^(-1/6)) or Thm. 2. The paper mentions supplementary diagnostics that I did not have access to.

summary: The manuscript proves (i) an explicit lower bound s_n >= exp(-3 sqrt(n)) for n >= 10^4, and s_n >= exp(-C sqrt(n)) for C > sqrt((8/3) log 17), for the residual inf over all unit-disk-root polynomials and complex slopes, via a finite Cesaro-type certificate; (ii) that the on-circle infimum tends to 1/sqrt(8) (Thm. 3); (iii) that one interior zero suffices to make the residual tend to zero, with rate O(n^(-1/6)) (Thm. 11); (iv) superalgebraic upper bounds with a fixed number of interior zeros (Thm. 2). The arithmetic of Sec. 3-4, Cor. 8, Cor. 9 and the algebra of Thm. 11 check out on inspection. The numerical check of Thm. 3 and Thm. 11 constructions supports the stated limits and identities. Theorem 2 is only outlined and its uniformity claims are asserted. The paper also has a minor algebra slip in Sec. 2 (missing factor z) and some sketched estimates in the Thm. 3 and Thm. 11 upper bounds. The novelty relative to the cited Tan et al. and Luo et al. results is as the paper claims, based on the abstracts I could read. Overall: careful, mostly checkable, with a substantive but incompletely verified Theorem 2 and sketchy estimates that need full write-up before the claims can be relied on.
strengths: Explicit, checkable finite certificate (Lemma 4, Lemma 5, Prop. 6) giving an explicit exp(-3 sqrt(n)) lower bound; the parameter choices in Sec. 4 and the numerics of eq. (12) verify.
Thm. 3 construction P_{m,k} has exact P'(0) = n/2 + 1/4 and P'(1)/P(1) = n/2, and the limiting integral 1/16 - 3/4*1/6 + 9/4*1/12 = 1/8 checks; numerically the residual approaches 1/sqrt(8).
Thm. 11 parameter system (eqs. 18-19 and the explicit X, Y, a, c) is internally consistent: the moment identities sum v^2 = 0 and sum v^3 = 0 follow from (18)-(19) and hold numerically.
Cor. 8 correctly derives a bound on exterior power sums from the Newton identity and the projection argument.
The paper is candid about what it does not prove (no optimal rates, no uniform constants in Thm. 2, no priority certification).
weaknesses: Theorem 2 (superalgebraic decay with a fixed number M_A of interior zeros) is only outlined: the implicit-function and Jacobian step, the claim that the moment system is solvable for all large n, and the uniform estimates are asserted, not shown. The constants depend on K and are not explicit.
The Thm. 3 upper-bound argument asserts the secondary-maximum inequality (1+c)^6/[729(1-c)^2] < 1 and the global bound on the outer arc without derivation.

Thm. 11: the claimed rate O(n^(-1/6)) is an upper bound only; the numerics I ran suggest a rate near n^(-0.21) over n in [3.4e3, 3.4e4], which does not decide the exponent. The local and outer estimates are sketched.
Sec. 2 identity B'/B - 3 = -3(z-1)^2/(z^3+1) omits a factor z; the correct form is -3z(z-1)^2/(z^3+1). The limit is unaffected.
Sec. 2 proof of the lower bound inf_lambda g_n(lambda) = 1/8 + O(1/n) uses a window argument (minimizers near n/2) whose justification is brief.
Literature: Komarov (arXiv:1804.08918, 1807.06499) and the other citations are described but I did not verify their statements; the paper itself says exhaustive priority certification is not claimed.
The paper relies on supplementary diagnostics that were not available to me; reproducibility of the large-n estimates depends on them.
potential_errors: Sec. 2, p. 3-4: B'_*/B_* - 3 = -3(z-1)^2/(z^3+1) should read -3z(z-1)^2/(z^3+1). Typographical/algebra slip; the limiting argument is unaffected.
Thm. 2 proof, p. 9-12: the claim that the local and outer estimates are uniform in n with constants depending only on K is asserted, not shown; treat as unverified rather than wrong.
strong_novelty_candidates: Explicit lower bound s_n >= exp(-3 sqrt(n)) for the unrestricted-slope residual over unit-disk-root polynomials (Thm. 1 with Prop. 6), strengthening the restricted-slope bound of Tan et al. (arXiv:2608.02043) as the paper states.
The sharp on-circle limit 1/sqrt(8) for both the unrestricted and restricted-slope infima (Thm. 3), with an explicit family P_{m,k} = B_t^m (1+z)^k.
One interior zero suffices for vanishing residual, with explicit algebraic parameters (Thm. 11), together with the zero-count threshold argument that combines Thm. 3 and Thm. 11.
